scope: Four alternative ASR editions of the same retained audio, evaluated in a counterfactual 25-source index. The released 25-source analysis and every existing source card remain unchanged.

model_comparison.previous: Existing Whisper tiny.en / multilingual tiny editions; source-specific receipts preserved
model_comparison.new_segmentation: Independent contiguous nonoverlapping windows of at most 30 seconds; final partial tails retained

method.lexical: Frozen baseline 25-source phrase mask, vocabulary and IDF; transform new text only, no refit on new editions.
method.semantic: Same pinned MiniLM model and complete 240-wordpiece pooling contract as the baseline.
method.recognition_disagreement: Exact unit-cost Levenshtein over NFKC/casefolded Unicode word tokens retaining numbers/apostrophes; divide by longer token sequence. Both sides are machine outputs, so this is not WER or accuracy.
method.canonical_audio: Exact same retained Opus and verified original 16 kHz mono s16le PCM sample hashes; Parakeet float inputs are derived from these same samples.
method.counterfactual: Replace only four rows for sensitivity calculations, retaining logical source IDs to compare neighbors. These matrices are not a new preferred corpus release.

card_reannotation.scope: Existing annotations remain bound to their unchanged old edition evidence. New wording and locators need independent reading before a new edition can inherit any card.

limitations: This changes the recognition pipeline, not just model weights: old Whisper VAD/context versus independent 30-second Parakeet windows, different decoding and punctuation behavior.
Same input samples do not make either machine transcript ground truth. More words or higher cosine do not prove higher accuracy.
Chunk boundaries can lose context or split speech; complete sample coverage does not establish complete or accurate recognized words.
Four purposely selected Council recordings do not represent all retained media, languages, channels or speaker styles.
The frozen lexical vocabulary treats new terms as out of vocabulary; scores measure a controlled representation change, not an improved topic model.
Existing question and claim cards are not automatically transferred to the new text. No agreement or contradiction label is changed by cosine.
